{{nihongo|'''Azumayanuma Shrine'''|東屋沼神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}{{ill|Fukushima (city)|an|Fukushima|ar|فوكوشيما (مدينة)|arz|فوكوشيما (تجمع سكان فى فوكوشيما)|az|Fukuşima|azb|فوکوشیما (شهر)|ban|Fukushima, Fukushima|bcl|Fukushima, Fukushima|be|Фукусіма (горад)|br|Fukushima (kêr)|ca|Fukushima (ciutat)|ce|Фукусима (гӀала)|ceb|Fukushima-shi (kapital sa prepektura sa Hapon)|ckb|فووکووشیما|cs|Fukušima|de|Fukushima (Fukushima)|el|Φουκουσίμα (πόλη)|eo|Fukuŝimo|es|Fukushima (Fukushima)|et|Fukushima|eu|Fukushima|fa|فوکوشیما (شهر)|fi|Fukushima|fr|Fukushima (ville de la préfecture de Fukushima)|frr|Fukushima|ga|Fukushima|gl|Fukushima|he|פוקושימה|hr|Fukushima|hu|Fukusima|hy|Ֆուկուսիմա (քաղաք)|id|Fukushima, Fukushima|is|Fukushima|it|Fukushima|ja|福島市|kn|ಫುಕುಷಿಮಾ|ko|후쿠시마시|ku|Fukushima|lt|Fukušima|lv|Fukusima|mg|Fukushima|mk|Фукушима|ml|ഫുക്കുഷിമ നഗരം|mr|फुकुशिमा|my|ဖူကူရှီးမားမြို့|mzn|فوکوشیما (شهر)|nl|Fukushima (stad)|no|Fukushima (Fukushima)|pl|Fukushima|pt|Fukushima (cidade)|ro|Fukushima|ru|Фукусима (город)|sc|Fukushima|scn|Fukushima|sh|Fukushima|simple|Fukushima (city)|sl|Fukušima, Fukušima|sq|Fukushima|sr|Фукушима|sv|Fukushima|sw|Fukushima, Fukushima|ta|புகுசிமா|tg|Фукушима|th|ฟูกูชิมะ (เมือง)|tl|Lungsod ng Fukushima|tr|Fukuşima|tt|Фукусима (шәһәр)|tw|Fukushima|uk|Фукусіма (Фукусіма)|ur|فوکوشیما|uz|Fukusima|vi|Fukushima (thành phố)|war|Fukushima (syudad)|wuu|福岛市|za|Fuzdauj Si|zh|福島市|zh_classical|福島市|zh_min_nan|Hukusima-chhī|zh_yue|福島市|qid=Q161176}}{{ill|iizakamachihirano|ja|飯坂町平野|qid=Q11666149}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was first classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} and later as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Azumayanuma Shrine'''|東屋沼神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

== History ==
According to the shrine’s origin record, the date of founding is unknown. In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} lists it as “{{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389}}{{ill|Shinobu district|ja|信夫郡|qid=Q11386050}} Azumayanuma Shrine, Myōjin Dai.” Among the five {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrines}} enshrined in Shinobu District (Azumayanuma Shrine, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Azumayakuni Shrine}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shirawase Shrine}}, {{ill|Kuronuma Shrine|ja|黒沼神社|qid=Q17228379}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kashima Shrine}}), it alone is designated as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}. It was also a site where the state ritual “Myōjin Festival” was conducted.

Before the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, it was regarded as the head shrine of the more than twenty villages in the Amari district located between the {{ill|Surikami River|Q11498645|qid=Q11498645}} and the {{ill|Matsukawa|Q11530259|qid=Q11530259|lt=Matsukawa}} flowing through present-day Fukushima City.

At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located near Kaminuma (Thunder Pond) on {{ill|Mount Azuma|Q2669374|qid=Q2669374}}. They were later relocated to Kioroshi-yama (Sacred Forest Mountain) in the {{ill|Ozaso|Q11438455|qid=Q11438455}} area at the foot of the mountain, and subsequently moved again to the present site. In ancient times, the shrine was known by various names, the main ones being as follows:

; “Nana-ō Daimyōjin”
: When the shrine was relocated to the Ōzaso area, seven targets were hung on trees within the shrine grounds for archery practice.
; “Nanamatsu Daimyōjin”
: Seven pine trees at the shrine were said to be inhabited by snakes that exterminated mice; these snakes were revered as messengers of the gods.
; “Azumayaharu Shrine”
: In the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=An’ei}}, {{ill|1781|Q7719|qid=Q7719}}, the name was given with the meaning that “through divine protection, the governance of the eastern lands (Azumaya) is brought to order.”

In {{ill|Meiji – year 2|Q11512277|qid=Q11512277}}, the shrine reverted to its present name, “Azumayanuma Shrine.” The museum within the shrine grounds preserves ridge tags, dedicatory plaques, photographs, and other materials from the periods when it was known as “Nana-ō Daimyōjin,” “Nanamatsu Daimyōjin,” and “Azumayaharu Shrine.”

In {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}}, under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in Meiji 8 it became a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. Today, it is chiefly worshipped as a deity of abundant harvests, protection from calamities, and fire prevention.

== Grounds ==
== Shrine buildings ==
The shrine complex consists of a haiden (worship hall), heiden (offering hall), and honden (main sanctuary).

'''Interior of the haiden'''

Behind the honden are stone miniature shrines, and within the grounds are a mikoshi storehouse, the Azumayanuma Shrine Museum, and playground equipment. Immediately behind the shrine buildings is {{ill|Hirano Station (Fukushima)|Q5769419|qid=Q5769419|lt=Hirano Station}} on the {{ill|Fukushima Kōtsū Iizaka Line|Q5507732|qid=Q5507732}}.
